title: Mitochondria affect antibacterial immunity in cross talk with innate immune response molecules coded by genes of nuclear origin.
authors: Chakraborty, Argha; Pal, Aruna; Debnath, Manti; Sahu, Jyoti; Pal, Abantika; Mukherjee, Joydeep; Samanta, Rajarshi; Chatterjee, Paresh Nath
one_liner_zh: 该文以鸭疫里氏杆菌感染为模型，结合分子对接和结构预测研究线粒体与核基因编码免疫蛋白的互作，虽涉及蛋白结构计算但对象非蛋白质结构核心问题，方法较基础，可部分借鉴其对接与结构预测流程。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Mitochondria are dynamic, semi-autonomous organelles that, in addition to their central role in ATP production, regulate calcium homeostasis, iron metabolism, apoptosis, and innate immune signalling. Although the mitochondrial genome encodes only 37 genes, mitochondrial architecture, bioenergetic function, and dynamics are governed predominantly by nuclear-encoded proteins, necessitating highly coordinated communication between mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and the nuclear genome. Disruption of this bidirectional mitochondrial-nuclear crosstalk has been increasingly implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous diseases across species; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying this communication remain incompletely understood. MATERIALS AND METHOD: In the present study, we used Anas platyrhynchos as a model of duck pasteurellosis to investigate mitochondrial-nuclear interactions in the regulation of innate immune responses during Pasteurella multocida infection. We characterized the mitochondrial (cytochrome b and cytochrome c) and nuclear genes (NLRP3, IL-18, and STING) of duck, in silico molecular docking, PHYRE 2 for PDB structure prediction, pymol visualization, and experimental validation with differential mRNA expression profiling. RESULT AND DISCUSSION: Our findings demonstrate that the mitochondrially encoded proteins cytochrome b and cytochrome c functionally interact with the nuclear-encoded immune regulators NLRP3, IL-18, and STING through the NOD-like receptor signalling pathway, phagocytic pathways, and the cytosolic DNA-sensing pathway. Furthermore, molecular docking analyses identified putative interaction sites between IL-18 and P. multocida, providing additional support for the functional relevance of these immune pathways during bacterial infection. To our knowledge, this study provides the first evidence in an animal model that mitochondrial retrograde signalling influences the regulation of nuclear immune genes during bacterial infection. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism through which mitochondrial gene products modulate host innate immune responses, thereby advancing our understanding of mitochondrial-nuclear communication in host-pathogen interactions.
abstract_zh: 引言：线粒体是动态、半自主的细胞器，除在ATP生成中发挥核心作用外，还调节钙稳态、铁代谢、细胞凋亡和先天免疫信号传导。尽管线粒体基因组仅编码37个基因，但线粒体结构、生物能量功能和动态主要受核编码蛋白控制，这要求线粒体DNA（mtDNA）与核基因组之间进行高度协调的通信。这种双向线粒体-核串扰的破坏日益被认为与多种物种中众多疾病的发病机制相关；然而，这种通信背后的分子机制仍未完全阐明。材料与方法：在本研究中，我们使用鸭（Anas platyrhynchos）作为鸭巴氏杆菌病模型，探讨多杀性巴氏杆菌感染期间线粒体-核相互作用在调节先天免疫反应中的作用。我们表征了鸭的线粒体基因（细胞色素b和细胞色素c）和核基因（NLRP3、IL-18和STING），进行了计算机模拟分子对接、使用PHYRE 2进行PDB结构预测、pymol可视化，并通过差异mRNA表达谱进行实验验证。结果与讨论：我们的研究结果表明，线粒体编码蛋白细胞色素b和细胞色素c通过NOD样受体信号通路、吞噬通路和胞质DNA感知通路，与核编码免疫调节因子NLRP3、IL-18和STING发生功能性相互作用。此外，分子对接分析确定了IL-18与多杀性巴氏杆菌之间的推定相互作用位点，为这些免疫通路在细菌感染期间的功能相关性提供了额外支持。据我们所知，本研究首次在动物模型中提供证据，表明细菌感染期间线粒体逆行信号影响核免疫基因的调节。这些发现揭示了一种先前未被识别的机制，通过该机制线粒体基因产物调节宿主先天免疫反应，从而增进了我们对宿主-病原体相互作用中线粒体-核通信的理解。
